research_scope: Additional source-free contextual alias confirmations from mathematically reviewed expression/object-type differences; retain source conditions and separate meanings.

aliases.reason: The topological coequalizer and set-valued diagram-colimit sources both use the smallest equivalence relation on a set containing a prescribed collection of ordered pairs. The topological quotient topology and the diagram indexing restrictions are additional source hypotheses, not part of equivalence-relation generation.

The pointwise continuity source separately refers to an open neighborhood U of x in X and V of f(x) in Y. Each is precisely an open subset containing the specified point; codomain versus domain and the function f are source-level parameters, not distinct neighborhood prerequisites.

Bourbaki-proper and universally closed map sources both require that an explicitly given continuous map send every closed subset to a closed subset of the target. Product versus fiber-product base changes are separate source constructions; no Hausdorffness or properness is inferred from the closed-map prerequisite.

The inverse-limit source uses the product of countably indexed R-modules, while the Mittag-Leffler source uses an arbitrary indexed product. Both are the direct-product module construction with coordinatewise operations; the countable indexing and inverse-limit compatibility equations remain source-specific.
